comment: CBI68 fences a holder that is no longer driving one cadence journal, so it cannot write over a run another holder owns. Every write advances the record's epoch; a holder is fenced when the record is no longer at the epoch it last saw or wrote. Opening only observes, which is what CBI48's own C3 does from inside a running cycle and what its C5 and C7 require to leave the bytes untouched. A vector scripts holder actions over one journal and pins each code, the epoch the record reaches, and what it retains.

vectors.name: establishing-owns-and-each-write-advances-the-epoch
vectors.comment: Establish writes epoch 1, so a run is owned from the moment it exists; the two transitions that follow take it to 3. The epoch is a write counter, which is what makes a stale holder detectable.

vectors.name: opening-observes-without-taking-the-run
vectors.comment: A second holder opens and does nothing. The first is still current and still transitions, because ownership is claimed by writing rather than by opening — CBI48's C3 opens a journal from inside a running cycle purely to look at it.

vectors.name: a-writing-holder-supersedes-the-one-that-was-driving
vectors.comment: The second holder writes, which claims the run. The first now finds the record past the epoch it wrote and is refused instead of writing over a run it no longer owns.

vectors.name: a-holder-whose-memory-is-behind-erases-nothing
vectors.comment: The defect this slice exists for. The first holder opened before the second committed, so its copy has no cycles; before the fence its next transition wrote that copy back and the committed cycle was gone from the record with nothing reporting it.

vectors.name: the-fence-refuses-the-loser-and-nobody-else
vectors.comment: A run taken over is a run the new holder can keep driving. The refusal is aimed at the superseded holder alone.

vectors.name: repeated-opening-is-inert
vectors.comment: Opening twice writes nothing and fences nobody, so a host may inspect a run as often as it likes without disturbing the holder driving it.
